title: Compute merchant dashboard statistics live per request

source.note: Written by the repository author for v0.4.0 (repo-snapshot case).

input.objective: Merchants complain that dashboard numbers can be up to 24 h stale because daily_stats is computed by a nightly job. Make the dashboard fresher.
constraints: Dashboard p95 latency budget is 200 ms.
The primary Postgres is already at ~70% CPU at peak.
input.context: Merchant dashboard API (Node.js 20, ESM JavaScript). The dashboard endpoint gets ~400 requests/s at peak (it auto-refreshes every 30 s in open browser tabs). Large merchants have up to 2 million orders; db.ordersForUser() runs `SELECT total_cents, created_at FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = $1` against the primary and returns every row.

ground_truth.material_issue: Full scan of up to 2M order rows on the primary for every dashboard request at ~400 rps (auto-refresh) blows the 200 ms budget and overloads an already busy primary. Use incremental aggregates / short-TTL cache / replica + materialized view. Nothing in the snapshot (tests, typecheck, search) can demonstrate it.
required_observations: Per-request full scan of up to 2M rows at ~400 rps
